subject: Prompt/response provenance, no-train scope, and evidence for subprocessors
messages:
From: Ian Turner <ian.turner@aventatherapeutics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aventa Legal <legal@aventatherapeutics.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Sep 2026 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Prompt/response provenance, no-train scope, and evidence for subprocessors

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Aventa's engineering and privacy teams had a few follow-ups around data handling that we need answered before we can advance the procurement checklist. High level: we need a contractual "no model training" commitment for any customer-provided prompts, attached files, and generated responses that contain PII or proprietary sequences.

Specific asks: 
- Can Redwood confirm whether hosted inference (your default API) is ever used to train models or improve models by default? If so, can that be contractually disabled (no-train)?
- We need explicit ownership language that our prompts + the model outputs remain Aventa IP (no claim to derivatives by Redwood).
- Please provide a current list of subprocessors and whether any subprocessors have access to raw prompts/responses. If possible, include their locations (country) and whether data is geofenced to the US/EU for our account.
- For KV/prefix caching: does Redwood persist cache entries server-side? Are those entries encrypted, and who controls the keys (customer KMS vs Redwood-managed)?
- Evidence: can you provide SOC 2 attestation, and an exportable spreadsheet showing last 90 days of subprocessor contracts or at least attestations?

We have a tight timeline — legal is asking for language and evidence by COB next Thursday (2026-09-12). I've attached a short questionnaire (Aventa_DPA_Questions_20260905.docx) to help structure responses.

Appreciate your help — happy to jump on a quick call if that's easier.

Regards,
Ian Turner
Head of IT Security
Aventa Therapeutics

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Prompt/response provenance, no-train scope, and evidence for subprocessors

Ian — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. Looping Dev from sales so we can get the legal/ops artifacts over. Below is a concise summary; we'll follow up with the artifacts and a short proposed clause you can share with counsel.

Summary answers (short):
- Training: Redwood's hosted inference does not use customer prompt/response content to retrain or fine-tune production models by default. We do collect telemetry (latency/usage/anonymous model health metrics) to operate the service. Customers may opt-in to a separate program that uses data for model improvement; that is NOT enabled unless contractually agreed.
- Contractual no-train: we offer a DPA addendum ("No-Train Addendum") that explicitly prohibits using your prompts/responses for model improvement or training. We'll attach a draft addendum for your review.
- Ownership: customers retain ownership of inputs and outputs; our standard language preserves customer IP for prompts and responses and excludes customer content from Redwood's derivative claims. We'll include the exact excerpt in the addendum.
- Subprocessors / geofencing: we'll provide a current subprocessor registry (name, primary country, role). For hosted customers we route services across regions for performance; if geofencing (US-only) is required we can support it via Dedicated or Private deployments, or via contractual data residency and contractual restrictions on subprocessor access for hosted accounts with enterprise agreements.
- KV/prefix cache: we use a short-lived KV cache to accelerate repeated prefixes. Cache entries are encrypted at rest. For enterprise customers we support customer-managed keys via KMS (bring-your-own-key) for certain Dedicated/Private plans; hosted customers may elect the no-train addendum and request additional protections — we will document the persistence windows and encryption in the evidence package.
- Evidence: we can provide a current SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), the subprocessor registry export, and an export-ready CSV of recent subprocessor attestations.

Next steps I'll take this week:
1) Attach: draft No-Train Addendum (redwood_no_train_addendum_v1.docx) and current subprocessor registry (subprocessors_2026Q3.csv).
2) Send: redacted SOC 2 Type II (SOC2_report_redacted.pdf) — ops/legal will prepare the redaction.
3) Propose: 30-minute handoff call between Aventa legal/engineering and our privacy/ops team — benched times below.

If that timeline works, Dev will get a DocuSign link ready for the DPA + addendum. If Aventa needs US-only geofencing for hosted we should mark that as a requirement in the SOW / contract and budget for potential dedicated capacity.

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions (Privacy & Compliance)
Redwood Inference

Kimberly — this is helpful, thanks. Quick clarifications before we take the addendum to our counsel: 

1) Can you paste the exact "no-train" sentence you plan to use (we want copy/paste into our redline).
2) For the KV cache: what's the default TTL (hours/days) and are cache entries ever written to persistent blob storage or only to encrypted ephemeral store?
3) Subprocessor access: can you indicate which subprocessors have the technical ability to access raw prompt/response content (not just metadata)? If any do, which ones and why?

If you can provide answers + the SOC2 redaction by EOD Thursday (2026-09-12), that will keep us on track for procurement. Also — please include any DocuSign link for the proposed addendum so our counsel can validate the doc.

Best,
Ian

Ian — thanks, sending the specific items Kimberly identified and a suggested clause excerpt below. Attaching the artifacts now.

Suggested no-train clause (excerpt you can drop into your DPA):
"Redwood Inference agrees that, unless Customer provides explicit, written consent, Customer Data (including prompts, files, and model outputs) will not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve any machine learning models or data products. Redwood will not incorporate Customer Data into model weights, training corpora, or derivative training datasets. Telemetry that is aggregated and anonymized for service operation (e.g., latency metrics) is excluded from this restriction."

KV cache specifics: default TTL = 6 hours for hosted inference; entries are stored in an encrypted, replicated in-memory cache backed by encrypted disk for failover (not used for long-term training). For enterprise Dedicated/Private customers we can provide a configuration to reduce TTL or disable cache persistence and support customer-managed keys.

Subprocessors with technical access to raw prompts/responses: only our logging/storage backend in the US (contracted provider: CloudStore Systems, LLC) and our monitoring provider for incident triage (LogSight Inc.) have roles that could access raw content in incident scenarios. Both are under contractual NDA and SOC2 obligations; neither uses data for model training. The attached CSV lists these providers, their primary country, and contractual role.

Attachments included: redwood_no_train_addendum_v1.docx, subprocessors_2026Q3.csv, SOC2_report_redacted.pdf

I'll also open a DocuSign envelope and share the link for the addendum and updated DPA so your counsel can preview. If you'd like a quick 30-min call, Lauren (our contracts lead) can join to walk through redlines. Available: Thu 09/16 11am ET or Fri 09/17 2pm ET.

Thanks — Dev
